newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude, gas oil futures gain in light trading.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude, gas oil futures gain in light trading.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures built slightly on their morning gains in light afternoon trade on Tuesday and were expected to hold steady, traders said.
Jan Brent was up 29 cents at $23.16 a barrel at 1540 GMT, just off its intraday high of $23.20, while Dec gas oil was up $2.75 at an intraday high of $221.50 a tonne.
"The market is up on pretty light trades," one trader said. "It's picked up rather than traded up."
The market was waiting on the latest inventory figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due to be released in New York later this evening, traders said.
Dealers in New York said the API may report a draw in total distillate stocks, which include heating oil, because of higher demand from last week's below normal temperature.
Industry analysts do not predict a heating oil shortage, but distillate inventories are low, with heating oil stocks a lean 14.5 million barrels below a year ago.
"If there were a draw anywhere...then we are going to see a little bit of a hike in prices," another trader said. "Otherwise, prices should stabilise and come off a little bit."
Traders said the market had also been buoyed by storms and cold weather across Europe, which was expected to continue through the weekend.
Volume remained relatively light in both the crude and gas oil futures markets, traders said, which made market sentiment difficult to gauge.
